why: A's fish 'from a river no man knew was there. it had been buried there, along with its world' is a thing that cannot arrive and does; B's empty-room simile is pretty but only restates the seed.
B turns the half-name into 'netherland' and has the deputy say 'i see one here that i married myself' — thin, but A is just two men shouting stock lines.
B's caller who dials the narrator's number insists 'It's my voice, she says. It's me.' — the own-number conceit arrives as a person; A dissolves into tea and toast on a green couch.
B stays in the uncanny letter by imagining the scene in the conditional ('clutched in his hand like a talisman'); A wanders off to an ink-stained trouser hem.
B keeps the dead tower and its line — 'it used to be the tower did the work' — while A slides into a stock post-plague dystopia with doll-faced children.

A: an arm dragged into the deep and eaten, 'it was the best thing that ever happened to me, and i felt like singing', then bones of old wood that make 'a new person, or a story'; B fragments into rain and grandmother.
Both hold the koan; A closes on the one voiceless thing speaking — 'the carrier said: hello.' — tighter than B's circling 'the student' loop.
B: 'i start crying, because i am not a boy' and the lights go out, the voice stops; A abandons the line for a chick-lit party with a lookalike named becky.
B keeps the brass as a live dread — 'now that it had once begun to ring, there was no knowing when it might not come again'; A turns it into a gold-and-envy fairy tale.
B's 'it doesn't eat me anymore' and the thing crawling the ceiling are meant, and it ends doubting itself; A is a google home and a hearing aid.
B pushes the anaphora into the dark — 'at night, my father is not my father... for I am not my daughter' — where A flattens into family memoir.
Both are eating-disorder realism; B keeps the 'it' that only looks like bread ('Tomorrow I will go back to eating bread'), A resolves it by sweeping up.
A holds the talking story — 'the story doesn't need to be saved. this story needs a mother.'; B breaks into a dated blog post and a stock prayer.
Neither: A adds a mr. johnstone to say nothing, B turns duncan into a sentimental reformer; the trial dialogue never gets stranger than the seed.
A collapses into a bandcamp 'Track Name:' footer; B at least finds a frame — 'we called him the body man' — though it's a war memoir, not the seed's spell.
A reasons in the seed's lunar logic — 'in consequence of the rarity of the matter on the moon, our houses... remained safe'; B drifts into a mountain etymology.
A keeps the spelling and the visitor: 'it seemed as if it was to speak and made no noyse'; B's 'I felt no fall at all' is good but it modernises.
B quotes Alice and becomes a blog post on rural sustainability; A at least stays in the children's-book night.
B brings the houses back as speakers — 'Where do you come from? Who are you?' asked the houses... 'We were all waiting for him'; A stops after one clause.
A answers the witch plainly — 'maybe the point of my existence is for you to exist.'; B turns into new-age incarnation copy.
B's writer 'was born in these hills, though i am told there was another life before... a cold wet blackness'; A writes a letter and names himself David.
A's talking mule ('Dang it. Now my coat has blood all over it.') is funny-broken, B is plain western; nothing meant arrives.
A's hair catches on 'something, someone, a thought' and rain makes the sky, earth, moon and stars talk; B is careful leaves and 'my mother says i am strange'.
A is set-theory lecture notes; B is a child's poem but keeps the question of names — 'i don't know what to call them except spider, mosquito.'
A holds the opium-eater voice and finds 'get snarled up and die like a sick spider in its own web'; B goes touring lemons at Civita-Vecchia.
B: 'the phone has no memory for anyone else', then reasons 'my father was sitting in a chair, which is not where he is now. that means it happened two days ago'; A turns into college nostalgia.
A keeps the groping-in-the-dark adventure and 'a presentiment... that something peculiar had happened'; B jumps to a boat and a crowd.
A cites David Mitchell and becomes a blog essay; B stays with the priests — 'there are endless cursors to blink for us all... it is always someone's turn.'
A: the phone can't say the name so 'it has no soul, and so no one else will either'; B is a boyfriend on the phone and an email.
A at least keeps the brass-witch and her brass sunk in a well; B forgets her for a Mary singing by the elderberries.

A rolls over the top and 'could hear my body falling down the other side, when instead of falling I found myself lying on a grassy slope' — dream-logic held in a child's voice; B is rain and hoofbeats.
B: 'you can feel all the potential in it. but the potential isn't actually very much, as everyone has forgotten the story that's supposed to go with it'; A becomes children taken to cells.
Both collapse into song lyrics; A's 'the voice of the silence keeps talking' is the one line that touches the seed, B writes 'chorus:'.
A: 'the hissing becomes words which become a story' and the story is of a woman given a computer and told to write one; B's lifts and outside things are good but plainer.
B is Secret Garden fanfic (martha, mary, mr. craven); A keeps the closed girl — an iron door with rust 'down her skinny legs like blood'.
B keeps the dreamer calling home — 'she would tell me to go back to my dream, that it was time to go back to work', from the moon; A is a good but generic free-verse memory.
Both are dream-report forum posts; A's civil-war tanks are funny-broken, B's aliens-or-ghosts is stock.
A stays in the body — 'at night they itch, and i know that they want to grow again'; B goes to ridiculous shoes then a fantasy story about Wren.
B turns into a blog 'updates' list; A, messy ('a cold winter's day in june'), still lands 'i was the ghost of her mother.'
A circles the same guilt; B moves — 'we needed someone to hate, because it's easier than hating ourselves' and 'at least i'd know my parents' names'.
Both strong; B's image is unforgettable — 'the noise of the moths flapping as they try and get out of its mouth' — and 'it lets me see him. his face, like mine'.
B's 'i wonder if this time there's an electric clock. it would be good to be able to hear time passing' implies a room returned to; A is a plain ward.
A keeps the head and the listening — 'i have tried to keep the head in the middle of them... the head has some use for words'; B becomes a folk tale about a lump of wood.
B's narrator 'played the same game i did when i was alive', and ghosts' skin burns in moonlight; A is a fine short close with the violet smell.
B keeps the father's names as a litany and ends 'i think that i am the only one in the whole world who knows where i am'; A drifts into mr. g and stroganoff.
A becomes court-record commentary; B holds a little longer — 'it was like a man and i saw its eyes, which was like a mans'.
A: 'it is she, not I, that I see in the mirror and I am happy'; B falls apart into disconnected lines.
B keeps the naming-by-action and makes it 'the dream of the ones who say goodbye'; A breaks into odd spacing and a friend's 'big live show'.
Close; A wins on the quieter impossibility — the house never answers, then 'when she answered, she sounded like the house.' B's 'if you hadn't gone and eaten him' is its equal in nerve.
A holds the inspector's report dead straight — 'the 20 lb. weight was not needed in the beginning, and was not added until after the test'; B turns into a fire story.
